clue.text: Miss rope that's cut

indicators.note: a rope that is cut loses its end, so the last letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: a lasso is a cowboy's noosed rope

explanation.surface: Someone misses a rope that has been severed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb but is the noun for a young woman; 'that's cut' drops the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is a girl or young woman, which is what lass means in northern and Scottish speech.

clue.text: Feller was upset after row

parts.note: a chain is a row or series of linked things

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word was is turned upside down, read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A man was distressed after an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' looks like slang for a man, but it is literally a thing that fells trees; 'upset' turns WAS into SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool that cuts down trees is a feller, and a powered toothed chain does exactly that job.

clue.text: Stay in favour of suspect in the middle

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: takes only the central letter of the word suspect

explanation.surface: A Cluedo-flavoured instruction: support the suspect who is caught in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a support or brace, the same as a structural support used to hold something up.

clue.text: Random policemen turning up to house heading to room with a detective

indicators.note: the reversed policemen hold the following pieces inside them, as a building houses people
in a down clue, the word for policemen is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: cops are policemen

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here taken from room

parts.note: DI is the abbreviation for Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: Officers head up to a mansion and into a room with a detective, as in a country-house murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes SPOC from COPS, which then houses R (heading to room), A and DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic events happen irregularly, at scattered and unpredictable intervals, much like random ones.

clue.text: See 7
Does it feature lead suspect, maiden and others?

parts.note: Mrs White is one of the six suspects in Cluedo
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
et al. is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: A Cluedo question: does the lead piping implicate a suspect, a young woman and others?
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the Cluedo weapon, the lead piping, but here it is the metal. Cluedo is the British name of the board game Clue.
explanation.definitionFit: White metal is any of several pale alloys, many of them containing lead along with tin or antimony.

clue.text: Is Rev Green bad, having taken a bent spanner?

indicators.note: the letter a is taken away from the fodder before it is rearranged
something bent is twisted out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the Reverend Green, the Cluedo suspect, wicked for having taken a crooked wrench?
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' looks like the tool (a wrench) but means something that spans. Rev Green is a Cluedo suspect; 'having taken' removes A from the fodder, and 'bent' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge spans a gap, so it is literally a spanner; this one crosses the Severn estuary between England and Wales.

clue.text: Place on board mostly for boss

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the Study is one of the rooms on the Cluedo board

explanation.surface: A spot on the board is chiefly for the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a manager, but here it is a raised knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round ornamental knob projecting from a surface, as a stud is.

clue.text: Despise men after act of violence

indicators.note: the men come after the act of violence in the answer

parts.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, a British criminal charge for assault
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: To scorn men after an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to loathe or detest it, the same strong dislike as despising.

clue.text: Document principally, Candlestick, Hall, Mrs …held by dad?

indicators.note: the initials sit inside the word for dad

parts.note: a dad is a parent

indicators.note: takes the principal, first, letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A Cluedo accusation listing a weapon, a room and a suspect, held by father.
explanation.walkthrough: The candlestick, the Hall and Mrs White or Peacock all belong to Cluedo, the British name of the game Clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is prepared animal skin used for writing, and by extension a document written on it.

clue.text: Led games going after Miss Scarlet?

indicators.note: the games come after the word for miss

parts.note: to skip something is to miss it out
PE, physical education, is school games
scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Someone captained games while pursuing Miss Scarlett from Cluedo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Scarlet' reads as the Cluedo suspect's name, but the two words do separate jobs; 'going after' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To skipper a team or ship is to captain it, so skippered means commanded or headed.

clue.text: Plod tense — do this in library?

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
reading is what one does in a library, also a Cluedo room

explanation.surface: A trudge through tense reading in the library.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to walk heavily, and to tread is likewise to step or walk with weight.

clue.text: See 25
Complete shock: winning

parts.note: a shock of hair is a mop
up means ahead, as a team that is winning is up

explanation.surface: A total surprise: victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to finish off the remaining work, so it means to complete a task.

clue.text: They don't put crosses on papers? Two good grades by markers?

definitions.text: They don't put crosses on papers?

parts.note: A and B are the top two exam grades
stainers leave marks on things

explanation.surface: Pupils who don't put crosses on exam papers get two good grades from the examiners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosses on papers' suggests marking exams; it means crosses on ballot papers. 'by' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: People who abstain in a vote do not mark a cross on a ballot paper.

clue.text: Vermin: essentially contains small mammals

indicators.note: the phrase before it contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Vermin, at heart, includes small mammals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' looks like the indicator for central letters, but it supplies the end of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoats in their white winter coats are called by this name, and stoats are small carnivorous mammals.

clue.text: Woman will fire shots from large gun

parts.note: she refers to a woman
'll is the short form of will

explanation.surface: A woman is going to fire shots from a big gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To shell a position is to bombard it with artillery, firing projectiles from heavy guns.

clue.text: Hand partners pieces on board

parts.note: a paw is a hand, informally
North and South are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: A bridge player hands the cards to partners, or moves pieces on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S, North and South, partner each other at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: On a chessboard the lowliest pieces are the eight small men in front of each army.

clue.text: Hint: stick in billiard room

definitions.meaning: a prompt or signal to act, as given to an actor
the rod used to strike balls, here in the Cluedo Billiard Room

explanation.surface: A clue: the stick in the billiard room.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is both a prompt that signals an action and the tapered stick used in billiards.

clue.text: Fit to take in ten clues to be solved

indicators.note: clues to be solved are puzzles to work out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ready to absorb ten clues that need solving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' looks like understanding, but here it means eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Esculent is a formal word for edible, so it describes food fit to be eaten.

clue.text: Hat in work held by peg

indicators.note: the work sits inside the peg

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A hat during work hangs on a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A topee is a light sun helmet of pith, worn in hot countries, so it is a kind of hat.

clue.text: Pounds to cover lives in retirement? Supported by these?

definitions.text: Pounds to cover lives in retirement? Supported by these?

indicators.note: the pounds surround the following pieces

parts.note: pens are pounds, enclosures for animals

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for lives is read backwards

parts.note: is means exists, lives
on means resting upon, supported by

explanation.surface: Money covers people living in retirement; are they supported by this income?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns only the word for lives backwards. The whole clue doubles as a description of retirement income.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular payments made to retired people cover their living costs, so retirees are supported by them.

clue.text: Peacock shows this? Best to decline

parts.note: a plum job is the best one
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: Mrs Peacock and Professor Plum of Cluedo are evoked: the finest is going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peacock' looks like the Cluedo suspect Mrs Peacock but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A peacock displays its feathers, and a bird's whole covering of feathers is called this.

clue.text: Result of competitions having missed lead piping

indicators.note: the lead, first letter, of the competitions word is missed out

parts.note: cups are trophy competitions
piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: The outcome of contests where the lead piping went missing, a Cluedo weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead piping' is the Cluedo weapon, but 'lead' belongs to the deletion and 'piping' means HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the final outcome of something, the eventual result.

clue.text: Preserve degree in wood frame

indicators.note: the degree sits inside the wood
the wood frames the degree, surrounding it

parts.note: elm is a wood
MBA is the Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: Keep a diploma in a wooden frame.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to treat it so it is preserved from decay.

clue.text: Last Cluedo room's empty? No suspect

definitions.text: Last Cluedo room's empty? No suspect

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or dodgy, so the letters are rearranged
an empty word keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: The last Cluedo room checked is empty, so nobody is suspected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' does double duty as anagram signal and definition: the result is one of the Cluedo suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Mustard is one of the six suspects in Cluedo, the game known as Clue in North America.

clue.text: Bowl balls without line and length at crease?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for both line and length
in cricket a batsman at the crease is in, batting

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction: bowl the balls on a good line and length to a batsman at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' looks like the cricket verb but is the noun for a dish. The crease is the line a batsman stands at.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a round open dish or vessel, so it is a type of bowl.

clue.text: Muscular admirer

definitions.meaning: informally, having a well-toned athletic body
an enthusiast or fan of something

explanation.surface: A brawny fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff is slang for physically fit and toned, and also an enthusiast, as in a film fan.

clue.text: Reports of things fired around home

indicators.note: the fired things go around the word for home

parts.note: bullets are fired from guns
in means at home

explanation.surface: Accounts of shots fired around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: News bulletins are short official reports or announcements.

clue.text: Goes out with European babes regularly

indicators.note: takes every other letter of babes, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone goes on dates with European beauties often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes out' sounds like dating, but it means the tide retreating.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbs when it flows back out to sea, so ebbs means recedes.

clue.text: Scene of murders in retreat

indicators.note: a retreating word goes backwards, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: to top someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: The site of killings, with the killers on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a place or location, the same as a scene where something happens.

clue.text: Cook, Prof … all on form for the Cluedo board?

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Cluedo line-up: Mrs White the cook and Professor Plum are all in form on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a person but is the anagram signal; 'Prof' and 'all on' are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cluedo board is laid out as a diagram of a house's rooms, a plan of one level of a building.

clue.text: That's it! Lose board game

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away, lose it
Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Eureka! Ditch the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is an exclamation of sudden success or discovery, like crying out on getting something right.
